title: Submission put on the forge
description: The body of the signed POST /v1/work-items/changes/submitted, application/json, with which an adapter reports what it put on the forge for a submission entry of the change feed (changes.schema.json): for each target of the entry that it handled, the address of each commit and, where the entry's target had draft, the draft. The control plane stores the addresses and the draft with the submission version, so the work item's pages link to them. It stores one reply for each target of a submission_id, identified by system and path, and keeps the first: a second reply for the same target, with the same content or another, is answered with a signed 204 and changes nothing. The adapter sends one reply for each submission entry, with a target for each target of the entry that did not fail, after it has addressed each commit and, for a target with draft, opened or updated the draft or left it as it was. It sends commits with every commit of the entry's target, and base with the address of base.commit. A target with draft in the entry has draft here: the draft after the adapter's call, with the title and the state that the draft has then. A target without draft in the entry has no draft here. A target that failed goes only to changes/failed (changes-failed.schema.json): it is not in this reply. A draft that a person closed or merged is reported with the action kept and its real state, closed or merged, and the adapter does not edit it. The same holds for an entry with draft.action open when such a draft already exists from the entry's branch: the adapter opens nothing and reports that draft. When the entry's draft.number matches no draft on the forge, the adapter reports the draft that it found from the branch, or the new one that it opened, so number may differ from the entry's. Every address is an https address of at most 2048 characters on the system of the target, with no user information, as definitions.schema.json, $defs.url, describes it. No two targets have the same system and path; the schema refuses only two identical items, and the control plane refuses a reply with a duplicate, 400 invalid_request. The control plane checks permissions first, in the order of refusal.schema.json: it returns 403 forbidden for a request the access key has no permission for. The request has no connection_id and no collection_ref, so connection_unknown, connection_ended, connection_suspended and collection_not_linked do not apply to it. The control plane returns a signed 204 and changes nothing for a submission_id that is not the submission_id of a submission entry in the adapter's change feed, and for a system and path that are not those of a target of that entry, so a repeated or late reply is never an error. A reply is refused 400 invalid_request when it contains a commit that the entry's target does not list or leaves one out, when a target has draft and the entry's target has none, when a target has no draft and the entry's target has one, and when it has a duplicate target. On success the control plane returns a signed 204 with no body. The adapter acts on each answer as follows. On the signed 204, it does not send the reply again. On 403 forbidden or 400 invalid_request, it stops sending the reply and logs the submission_id. On a transient failure, no answer, a 5xx or an unsigned answer, it sends the reply again, built anew as definitions.schema.json describes a retry, with backoff, and on a signed 429 it waits the seconds of Retry-After first. It stops sending the reply once its retries end, and logs the submission_id. The adapter logs no title, description or access key. The request is signed with the adapter's access key as definitions.schema.json describes. Set time from the adapter's clock and sign each request anew: the control plane returns an unsigned 401 for a time more than 300 seconds off its clock, either way, and for a request whose signature it has already seen; definitions.schema.json has the replay rule. Send only the members this schema defines: the control plane returns 400 invalid_request for any other member.

version.description: The document format. Set it to 1: the control plane returns 400 invalid_request for any other version.

time.description: When the adapter built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. Set it from the adapter's clock: the control plane returns an unsigned 401 for a time more than 300 seconds off its clock, either way.

submission_id.description: The submission_id of the submission entry that the adapter is reporting on.

targets.description: The targets of the entry that the adapter handled, 1 to 20. No two targets have the same system and path; the schema refuses only two identical items, and the control plane refuses any other duplicate, 400 invalid_request.

target.description: What the adapter put on the forge for one repository of the entry.

system.description: The system of the repository, as the entry has it. It has no port, as the entry's system.

path.description: The path of the repository, as the entry has it.

base.description: The address of the base commit: the commit of base.commit in the entry.

commit.description: The commit, as the entry lists it.

commit_url.description: The forge's address of the commit.

commits.description: One item for each commit that the entry's repository lists, in the entry's order, 1 to 100.

commit.description: The commit, as the entry lists it.

commit_url.description: The forge's address of the commit.

draft.description: The draft after the adapter's call. Present exactly when the entry's target has draft.

number.description: The draft's number on the forge, 1 or more. It may differ from the number in the entry, which is a hint: see draft.number in changes.schema.json.

url.description: The draft's address on the forge.

title.description: The draft's title after the call, by the rule of $defs.draft_title in definitions.schema.json: 1 to 256 characters on one line.

state.description: draft: the forge shows the draft as not ready for review. open: it shows it as ready for review. closed: a person closed it without merging it. merged: it was merged. The adapter edits only a draft that is draft or open.

action.description: opened: the adapter opened the draft. updated: it changed the draft's title or description. kept: it changed nothing, because the draft was closed or merged, or because it already had the entry's block and a title that the rule of previous_title leaves as it is. A closed or merged draft always has kept.
